title: Terminal extra-degeneracy realization is a weak equivalence in a simplicial model category
statement:
Use the simplicial model terminology of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], the Reedy model structure of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], and the simplex category and simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a simplicial model category with its Reedy model structure on simplicial objects. A simplicial object is a functor $X_\bullet:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal M$, and an augmentation to an object $Y\in\mathcal M$ is a natural transformation $X_\bullet\to\operatorname{const}Y$. Let such an augmented simplicial object have Reedy-cofibrant underlying simplicial object $X_\bullet$, and write $\varepsilon:X_0\to Y$ for its degree-zero augmentation. Suppose there are maps $t_{-1}:Y\to X_0$ and $t_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ satisfying the terminal extra-degeneracy identities $d_{n+1}t_n=1$, $d_0t_0=t_{-1}\varepsilon$, $d_it_n=t_{n-1}d_i$ for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$, $s_it_n=t_{n+1}s_i$ for $0\leq i\leq n$, and $\varepsilon t_{-1}=1$. Then the realization map $|X_\bullet|:=\int^{[n]\in\Delta}X_n\otimes\Delta^n\to Y$ induced by the augmentation is a weak equivalence in $\mathcal M$. No fibrancy or nonemptiness assumption on $Y$ is required. Here $\Delta^n=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(-,[n])$, and the displayed coend is the coequalizer of the two maps
$$\coprod_{\alpha:[m]\to[n]}X_n\otimes\Delta^m\rightrightarrows\coprod_{[n]\in\Delta}X_n\otimes\Delta^n,$$
one induced by $X(\alpha):X_n\to X_m$ and the other by $\Delta^\alpha:\Delta^m\to\Delta^n$; $\otimes$ is the simplicial tensor.

source.place: Dugger, A Primer on Homotopy Colimits, Definition 3.11 and Proposition 3.12 (sinklike contracting homotopy), printed pp.12-13; Section 19.1, printed p.90, for its simplicial-model-category extension. Read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category realization theorem.

proof.text: Define $r:\Delta\to\Delta$ by $r[n]=[n]$ and $r(\alpha)(i)=n-\alpha(m-i)$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$. Reversing both orders preserves monotonicity, $r(\beta\alpha)=r(\beta)r(\alpha)$, and $r^2=1$. For $Z=X\circ r^{\mathrm{op}}$, the faces are $d_i^Z=d_{n-i}^X$ on $Z_n$ and the degeneracies are $s_i^Z=s_{n-i}^X$ on $Z_n$. Set $h_n=t_n$ and $h_{-1}=t_{-1}$. The given identities become $d_0^Zh_n=1$, $d_1^Zh_0=t_{-1}\varepsilon$, $d_{i+1}^Zh_{n+1}=h_nd_i^Z$, and $s_{i+1}^Zh_n=h_{n+1}s_i^Z$; for example the last identity is the given $s_{n-i}^Xt_n=t_{n+1}s_{n-i}^X$. Thus these are first-face extra-degeneracy data on $Z$, with the original augmentation.

Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism] to $Z$ and these $h_n$. It supplies $a_n=Z(q_n)t_{-1}$, $\varepsilon a=1$, and prism maps $K_j^n:Z_n\to Z_{n+1}$ with $d_0^ZK_0^n=1$ and $d_{n+1}^ZK_n^n=a_n\varepsilon_n$. The unique $q_n:[n]\to[0]$ is fixed by $r$, so $a_n=X(q_n)t_{-1}$ is also a simplicial section for $X$. Put $H_j^n=K_{n-j}^n$. Then $d_0^XH_0^n=a_n\varepsilon_n$ and $d_{n+1}^XH_n^n=1$. Substituting $i\mapsto n+1-i$ and $j\mapsto n-j$ in the face prism relations for $K$ interchanges their two strict-inequality cases and preserves the middle equality; substituting $i\mapsto n+1-i$ in the degeneracy relations interchanges their two cases. Hence $H$ is a combinatorial homotopy connecting $1_X$ to $a\varepsilon$. The section is formed with ordinary degeneracies, not by iterating the $t_n$.

By [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], $X_0$ is cofibrant. Since $\varepsilon_0t_{-1}=1_Y$, the initial arrow to $Y$ is a retract of the initial arrow to $X_0$, and the retract axiom makes $Y$ cofibrant. The constant diagram $\operatorname{const}Y$ is Reedy-cofibrant: its degree-zero latching object is initial; for $n>0$ the latching indexing category is nonempty and connected because the unique surjection $[n]\twoheadrightarrow[0]$ maps to every other surjection in the opposite indexing category. A constant diagram on such an index has colimit $Y$, so its latching map is $1_Y$. Cofibrations include identities by the lifting-property definition in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization].

Apply [lem-coef-reedy-realization-homotopy-invariance] to $f=\varepsilon:X\to\operatorname{const}Y$ and $g=a$. Step 3 verifies both Reedy-cofibrancy assumptions. Step 2 supplies the combinatorial homotopy between $gf$ and $1_X$; for $fg=1$ the constant prism homotopy has degree-raising maps $s_j$ (all identity maps on the constant object). Therefore $|\varepsilon|:|X|\to|\operatorname{const}Y|$ is a weak equivalence. Finally $|\operatorname{const}Y|\cong Y$: the map to $Y$ collapses each $\Delta^n$ to $\Delta^0$, and the inverse is inclusion of the degree-zero summand $Y\otimes\Delta^0\cong Y$. The coend relation for $q_n:[n]\to[0]$ identifies every degree-$n$ inclusion with this inverse after collapse, so the composites are identities. Under this isomorphism $|\varepsilon|$ is exactly the augmentation-induced map in the statement. No fibrancy or nonemptiness is used.

proof_origin.place: Second-reader proof of Proposition 3.12 in the simplicial model setting of Section 19.1, using the exact general-category Mathlib extra-degeneracy homotopy. Dugger leaves the contraction argument as an exercise; the index reversal, correct section and cofibrancy checks are written here.
